[125](https://docs.rs#125)
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    /// Formats the number into a string
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    pub fn format(&self, value: f64) -> String {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)        // Handle non-finite values explicitly to avoid loops in scaling logic
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        if value.is_nan() {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)            return "NaN".to_owned();
[131](https://docs.rs#131)        }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)
[133](https://docs.rs#133)        if value < 0.0 {
[134](https://docs.rs#134)            return format!("-{}", self.format(-value));
[135](https://docs.rs#135)        }
[136](https://docs.rs#136)
[137](https://docs.rs#137)        if value.is_infinite() {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)            return "inf".to_owned();
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)
[141](https://docs.rs#141)        // If a forced suffix is provided, attempt to scale to that suffix
[142](https://docs.rs#142)        let scaled_value = if !self.forced_suffix.is_empty() {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)            // normalize micro sign in forced suffix when looking up
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            let lookup = self.forced_suffix.replace('\u{00B5}', "u");
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            match self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&lookup) {
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                Ok(mult) => ScaledValue {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                    value: value / mult,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)                    suffix: self.forced_suffix.clone(),
[149](https://docs.rs#149)                },
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                Err(_) => self.scales.to_scaled_value(value),
[151](https://docs.rs#151)            }
[152](https://docs.rs#152)        } else {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)            self.scales.to_scaled_value(value)
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        };
[155](https://docs.rs#155)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)        let out_suffix = if self.use_micro_sign && scaled_value.suffix == "u" {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            "µ".to_owned()
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        } else {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            scaled_value.suffix.clone()
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        };
[161](https://docs.rs#161)
[162](https://docs.rs#162)        format!(
[163](https://docs.rs#163)            "{:.width$}{}{}{}",
[164](https://docs.rs#164)            scaled_value.value,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)            self.separator,
[166](https://docs.rs#166)            out_suffix,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)            self.forced_units,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)            width = self.decimals
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        )
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    /// Parse a string back into a float value.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    ///
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    /// This convenience wrapper unwraps the result of `try_parse` and will panic
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    /// on malformed input. It is feature-gated behind `panic_parse` so that
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// consumers must opt-in to the panicking API via the panic_parse feature.
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    #[cfg(feature = "panic_parse")]
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    #[deprecated(
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        note = "Use `try_parse`, which returns `Result<f64, ParseError>` and does not panic on malformed input"
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    )]
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    pub fn parse(&self, value: &str) -> f64 {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        self.try_parse(value).unwrap()
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    }
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// Attempt to parse a string back into a float value.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    ///
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// Examples:
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    ///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    /// ```rust
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    /// // SI example
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    /// let f = Formatter::new();
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    /// assert_eq!(f.try_parse("1.00 k").unwrap(), 1000.0);
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    /// // Binary scales (Ki = 1024)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// let mut fbin = Formatter::new();
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// fbin.with_scales(Scales::Binary());
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// assert_eq!(fbin.try_parse("1.00 Ki").unwrap(), 1024.0);
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// // Units specified via with_units() are automatically stripped from input
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// let mut funit = Formatter::new();
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// funit.with_units("B");
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// assert_eq!(funit.try_parse("1.00 kB").unwrap(), 1000.0);
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// // Negative numbers
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// assert_eq!(Formatter::new().try_parse("-1.0 k").unwrap(), -1000.0);
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// // Invalid input
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// assert!(Formatter::new().try_parse("bad input").is_err());
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// ```
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    pub fn try_parse(&self, value: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        let (number_str, suffix) = self.parse_components(value)?;
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        let number = number_str
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            .parse::<f64>()
[211](https://docs.rs#211)            .map_err(ParseError::InvalidNumber)?;
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        let magnitude_multiplier = self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&suffix)?;
[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)        Ok(number * magnitude_multiplier)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    fn parse_components(&self, value: &str) -> Result<(String, String), ParseError> {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        // Remove forced units if present
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        let value = value
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            .trim()
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            .trim_end_matches(&self.forced_units)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            .to_string();
[223](https://docs.rs#223)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        // Extract leading number (allow sign and decimal)
[225](https://docs.rs#225)        let mut number = String::new();
[226](https://docs.rs#226)        for (i, c) in value.chars().enumerate() {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)            if c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.' || (c == '-' && i == 0) {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                number.push(c);
[229](https://docs.rs#229)            } else {
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                break;
[231](https://docs.rs#231)            }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        }
[233](https://docs.rs#233)
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        if number.is_empty() {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            return Err(ParseError::EmptyInput);
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        }
[237](https://docs.rs#237)
[238](https://docs.rs#238)        let suffix = value
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            .trim_start_matches(&number)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            .trim_start_matches(&self.separator)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            .to_string();
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        // Normalize common variants: acceptance of micro sign 'µ'
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        let suffix = suffix.replace('\u{00B5}', "u");
[245](https://docs.rs#245)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        Ok((number, suffix))
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    }
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// Parse a string and optionally clamp unknown suffixes to the largest suffix multiplier.
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    ///
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    /// If `clamp` is `false`, this behaves like `try_parse` and returns an error on unknown suffixes.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    /// If `clamp` is `true`, unknown suffixes will be interpreted as the largest available suffix.
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    ///
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// Examples:
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    ///
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// ```rust
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    /// let f = Formatter::new();
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    /// // Unknown suffix errors when clamp == false
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", false).is_err());
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// // Unknown suffix clamps to largest suffix multiplier when clamp == true
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", true).is_ok());
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// // Binary example with units
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    /// let mut fb = Formatter::new();
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// fb.with_scales(Scales::Binary()).with_units("B");
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    /// assert_eq!(fb.parse_or_clamp("1.0 KiB", false).unwrap(), 1024.0);
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    /// // Negative number with clamp
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// assert_eq!(Formatter::new().parse_or_clamp("-1.0 k", true).unwrap(), -1000.0);
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// ```
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    pub fn parse_or_clamp(&self, value: &str, clamp: bool) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        let (number_str, suffix) = self.parse_components(value)?;
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        let number = number_str
[273](https://docs.rs#273)            .parse::<f64>()
[274](https://docs.rs#274)            .map_err(ParseError::InvalidNumber)?;
[275](https://docs.rs#275)
[276](https://docs.rs#276)        match self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&suffix) {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            Ok(mult) => Ok(number * mult),
[278](https://docs.rs#278)            Err(ParseError::UnknownSuffix(_)) if clamp => {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                // If scales has an explicit_map (e.g., Time), clamp to the
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                // largest explicit multiplier rather than assuming a power of
[281](https://docs.rs#281)                // `base` matching the last suffix index.
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                if let Some(map) = &self.scales.explicit_map
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                    && !map.is_empty()
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                    let max_mult = map.values().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                    return Ok(number * max_mult);
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                }
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                let last_index = self.scales.suffixes.len().saturating_sub(1);
[290](https://docs.rs#290)                let mult = (self.scales.base as f64).powi(last_index as i32);
[291](https://docs.rs#291)
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                Ok(number * mult)
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            }
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            Err(e) => Err(e),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        }
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    }
[297](https://docs.rs#297)}
[298](https://docs.rs#298)
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// Errors returned by parsing operations.
[300](https://docs.rs#300)#[derive(Debug)]
[301](https://docs.rs#301)pub enum ParseError {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    EmptyInput,
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    InvalidNumber(std::num::ParseFloatError),
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    UnknownSuffix(String),
[305](https://docs.rs#305)}
[306](https://docs.rs#306)
[307](https://docs.rs#307)impl PartialEq for ParseError {
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
[309](https://docs.rs#309)        match (self, other) {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            (ParseError::EmptyInput, ParseError::EmptyInput) => true,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            // Note: `ParseFloatError` does not implement `PartialEq` on stable Rust.
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            // We therefore treat all `InvalidNumber(_)` variants as equal to each other,
[313](https://docs.rs#313)            // ignoring the inner `ParseFloatError`.
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            (ParseError::InvalidNumber(_), ParseError::InvalidNumber(_)) => true,
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            (ParseError::UnknownSuffix(a), ParseError::UnknownSuffix(b)) => a == b,
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            _ => false,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)}
[320](https://docs.rs#320)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)impl std::fmt::Display for ParseError {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        match self {
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            ParseError::EmptyInput => write!(f, "Empty input"),
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            ParseError::InvalidNumber(e) => write!(f, "Invalid number: {}", e),
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            ParseError::UnknownSuffix(s) => write!(f, "Unknown suffix: {}", s),
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    }
[329](https://docs.rs#329)}
[330](https://docs.rs#330)
[331](https://docs.rs#331)impl std::error::Error for ParseError {}
[332](https://docs.rs#332)
[333](https://docs.rs#333)impl Default for Scales {
[334](https://docs.rs#334)    fn default() -> Self {
[335](https://docs.rs#335)        Scales::SI()
[336](https://docs.rs#336)    }
[337](https://docs.rs#337)}

[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// Instantiates a new `Scales` for time units.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    ///
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// This maps common time suffixes to multipliers in seconds.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    #[allow(non_snake_case)]
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    pub fn Time() -> Self {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        use std::collections::HashMap;
[410](https://docs.rs#410)
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        let mut map: HashMap<String, f64> = HashMap::new();
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        map.insert("ns".to_owned(), 1e-9);
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        map.insert("us".to_owned(), 1e-6);
[414](https://docs.rs#414)        map.insert("ms".to_owned(), 1e-3);
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        map.insert("s".to_owned(), 1.0);
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        map.insert("m".to_owned(), 60.0);
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        map.insert("h".to_owned(), 3600.0);
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        map.insert("d".to_owned(), 86400.0);
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        map.insert("w".to_owned(), 604800.0);
[420](https://docs.rs#420)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        // longer period units using average definitions
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        let year_secs = 365.2425 * 86400.0; // average Gregorian year
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        let month_secs = year_secs / 12.0; // average month
[424](https://docs.rs#424)
[425](https://docs.rs#425)        map.insert("mo".to_owned(), month_secs);
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        map.insert("month".to_owned(), month_secs);
[427](https://docs.rs#427)
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        // quarters: three-month periods
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        map.insert("qtr".to_owned(), 3.0 * month_secs);
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        map.insert("y".to_owned(), year_secs);
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        map.insert("yr".to_owned(), year_secs);
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        map.insert("year".to_owned(), year_secs);
[433](https://docs.rs#433)
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        map.insert("dec".to_owned(), 10.0 * year_secs);
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        map.insert("decade".to_owned(), 10.0 * year_secs);
[436](https://docs.rs#436)
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        map.insert("c".to_owned(), 100.0 * year_secs);
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        map.insert("century".to_owned(), 100.0 * year_secs);
[439](https://docs.rs#439)
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        map.insert("kyr".to_owned(), 1000.0 * year_secs); // millennium (kilo-year)
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        map.insert("millennium".to_owned(), 1000.0 * year_secs);
[442](https://docs.rs#442)
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        map.insert("Myr".to_owned(), 1.0e6 * year_secs);
[444](https://docs.rs#444)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        map.insert("Gyr".to_owned(), 1.0e9 * year_secs);
[446](https://docs.rs#446)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        Scales {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)            base: 1,
[449](https://docs.rs#449)            suffixes: vec![],
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            suffixes_neg: vec![],
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            explicit_map: Some(map),
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        }
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    }

[461](https://docs.rs#461)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    /// Sets the suffixes listing appropriately
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    pub fn with_suffixes(&mut self, suffixes: Vec<&str>) -> &mut Self {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        self.suffixes = Vec::new();
[465](https://docs.rs#465)
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        for suffix in suffixes {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)            // This should be to_owned to be clear about intent.
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            // https://users.rust-lang.org/t/to-string-vs-to-owned-for-string-literals/1441/6
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            self.suffixes.push(suffix.to_owned());
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        }
[471](https://docs.rs#471)
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        self
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    }
[474](https://docs.rs#474)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    fn try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&self, value: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        // If an explicit mapping exists (e.g., time units), prefer it
[477](https://docs.rs#477)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map
[478](https://docs.rs#478)            && let Some(val) = map.get(value)
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        {
[480](https://docs.rs#480)            return Ok(*val);
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        }
[482](https://docs.rs#482)
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        // positive suffixes
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        if let Some((idx, _)) = self.suffixes.iter().enumerate().find(|(_, x)| x == &value) {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)            return Ok((self.base as f64).powi(idx as i32));
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        }
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        // negative suffixes (fractions)
[489](https://docs.rs#489)        if let Some((idx, _)) = self
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            .suffixes_neg
[491](https://docs.rs#491)            .iter()
[492](https://docs.rs#492)            .enumerate()
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            .find(|(_, x)| x == &value)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            // idx 0 corresponds to base^0 (no scaling); idx 1 => base^-1, idx 2 => base^-2
[496](https://docs.rs#496)            let exp = -(idx as i32);
[497](https://docs.rs#497)            return Ok((self.base as f64).powi(exp));
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        }
[499](https://docs.rs#499)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        // build valid suffix list for error message
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        let mut valid: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map {
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            valid.extend(map.keys().cloned());
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        }
[505](https://docs.rs#505)
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        valid.extend(
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            self.suffixes
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                .iter()
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                .filter(|x| !x.trim().is_empty())
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                .cloned(),
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        );
[512](https://docs.rs#512)
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        valid.extend(
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            self.suffixes_neg
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                .iter()
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                .filter(|x| !x.trim().is_empty())
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                .cloned(),
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        );
[519](https://docs.rs#519)
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        Err(ParseError::UnknownSuffix(format!(
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            "{}; valid suffixes are: {}",
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            value,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            valid.join(", ")
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        )))
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    fn to_scaled_value(&self, value: f64) -> ScaledValue {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)        let mut index: usize = 0;
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        let base: f64 = self.base as f64;
[530](https://docs.rs#530)        let mut value = value;
[531](https://docs.rs#531)
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        // Prevent infinite loops for non-finite values and cap index to available suffixes
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let last_index = self.suffixes.len().saturating_sub(1);
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        let last_neg = self.suffixes_neg.len().saturating_sub(1);
[535](https://docs.rs#535)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)        // If explicit map provided (e.g., Time), prefer selecting suffix from it
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            // Build vector of (suffix, multiplier) and sort descending by multiplier
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            let mut entries: Vec<(String, f64)> =
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                map.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), *v)).collect();
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            entries.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
[542](https://docs.rs#542)
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            if value > 0.0 {
[544](https://docs.rs#544)                for (suf, mult) in entries.iter() {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                    if value >= *mult {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)                        return ScaledValue {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)                            value: value / *mult,
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                            suffix: suf.clone(),
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                        };
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                    }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                // If smaller than smallest multiplier, use smallest (e.g., ns)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                if let Some((suf, mult)) = entries.last() {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                    return ScaledValue {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                        value: value / *mult,
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                        suffix: suf.clone(),
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                    };
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        }
[562](https://docs.rs#562)
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        if value >= base {
[564](https://docs.rs#564)            while value >= base && index < last_index {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)                value /= base;
[566](https://docs.rs#566)                index += 1;
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)
[569](https://docs.rs#569)            ScaledValue {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)                value,
[571](https://docs.rs#571)                suffix: self.suffixes[index].to_owned(),
[572](https://docs.rs#572)            }
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        } else if value > 0.0 && value < 1.0 {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            // Use negative prefixes for fractional values
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            let mut neg_idx: usize = 0;
[576](https://docs.rs#576)            while value < 1.0 && neg_idx < last_neg {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                value *= base;
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                neg_idx += 1;
[579](https://docs.rs#579)            }
[580](https://docs.rs#580)
[581](https://docs.rs#581)            ScaledValue {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                value,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                suffix: self.suffixes_neg[neg_idx].to_owned(),
[584](https://docs.rs#584)            }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)        } else {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)            ScaledValue {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                value,
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                suffix: self.suffixes[0].to_owned(),
[589](https://docs.rs#589)            }
[590](https://docs.rs#590)        }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    }
[592](https://docs.rs#592)}

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#120-124)

#### pub fn [with_micro_sign](https://docs.rs#method.with_micro_sign)(&mut self, enable: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut Self

Enable using the micro sign `µ` in formatted output when fractional suffix is `u`.

Attempt to parse a string back into a float value.

Examples:

```
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
// SI example
let f = Formatter::new();
assert_eq!(f.try_parse("1.00 k").unwrap(), 1000.0);
// Binary scales (Ki = 1024)
let mut fbin = Formatter::new();
fbin.with_scales(Scales::Binary());
assert_eq!(fbin.try_parse("1.00 Ki").unwrap(), 1024.0);
// Units specified via with_units() are automatically stripped from input
let mut funit = Formatter::new();
funit.with_units("B");
assert_eq!(funit.try_parse("1.00 kB").unwrap(), 1000.0);
// Negative numbers
assert_eq!(Formatter::new().try_parse("-1.0 k").unwrap(), -1000.0);
// Invalid input
assert!(Formatter::new().try_parse("bad input").is_err());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#270-296)#### pub fn [parse_or_clamp](https://docs.rs#method.parse_or_clamp)(
    &self,
    value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    clamp: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#270-296)

#### pub fn [parse_or_clamp](https://docs.rs#method.parse_or_clamp)(
    &self,
    value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    clamp: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)>

Parse a string and optionally clamp unknown suffixes to the largest suffix multiplier.

If `clamp` is `false`, this behaves like `try_parse` and returns an error on unknown suffixes.
If `clamp` is `true`, unknown suffixes will be interpreted as the largest available suffix.

Examples:

```
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
let f = Formatter::new();
// Unknown suffix errors when clamp == false
assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", false).is_err());
// Unknown suffix clamps to largest suffix multiplier when clamp == true
assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", true).is_ok());
// Binary example with units
let mut fb = Formatter::new();
fb.with_scales(Scales::Binary()).with_units("B");
assert_eq!(fb.parse_or_clamp("1.0 KiB", false).unwrap(), 1024.0);
// Negative number with clamp
assert_eq!(Formatter::new().parse_or_clamp("-1.0 k", true).unwrap(), -1000.0);
```

# human_format - Rust

## Expand description

`human_format` is a library for formatting numbers into human readable strings. It supports SI, Time and Binary scales out of the box, and allows for custom scales as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#setup)Setup

Add the library to your dependencies listing

`$ cargo add human_format`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Print human readable strings from numbers using SI scales by default

```
// "1.00 k"
let tmpStr = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000.0);
// "1.00 M"
let tmpStr2 = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000000.0);
// "1.00 G"
let tmpStr3 = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000000000.0);
```
If you are so inspired you can even try playing with units and customizing your `Scales`

For more examples you should review the examples on github: [tests/demo.rs](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/blob/master/tests/demo.rs)

# human_format 1.2.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/human_format/1.2.0

# human_format

Rust Port of human-format from node, formatting numbers for us, while the machines are still at bay.

| Main | Develop |
|---|---|

`human_format` is a small Rust library that makes numbers easier for people to read. It converts large or small numbers into short strings, like turning `1_000_000` into "1.00 M".

## What it does

- Formats numbers with familiar suffixes: `k`,`M`,`G`, and so on.
- Parses human-friendly strings back into numbers with `try_parse`.
- Supports the newest SI prefixes (`R`,`Q`,`r`,`q`).
- Accepts and (optionally) outputs the micro sign `µ`.
- Lets you force a specific suffix for output (for example, always show values in `M`).
- Includes a `Scales::Time()`option for common time units (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months, years, quarters, centuries, etc.).

## Quick start

Add the crate:

```
```
Use the formatter:

```
use Formatter;
// Default SI formatting
let s = new.format;
assert_eq!;
// Control decimals
let s = new.with_decimals.format;
assert_eq!;
```
Use binary scales (base 1024):

```
use ;
let s = new.with_scales.format;
assert_eq!;
```
## Parsing strings

Convert a human-friendly string back to a `f64` with `try_parse`.

```
use ;
let f = new;
assert_eq!;
let mut fb = new;
fb.with_scales;
assert_eq!;
```
The parser accepts the micro sign `µ` as input.

## Force a suffix in output

To force output to a certain suffix, use `with_suffix`. The value is scaled to match that suffix if possible.

```
use Formatter;
let mut f = new;
f.with_suffix;
assert_eq!;
```
If the suffix is not valid for the current `Scales`, the formatter falls back to automatic selection.

## Micro sign output

Use `with_micro_sign(true)` to show `µ` for micro values in the output.

```
use Formatter;
let mut f = new;
f.with_micro_sign;
assert_eq!;
```
Parsing accepts both `u` and `µ`.

## Time scales

`Scales::Time()` uses a set of explicit unit multipliers for time. It uses average values where needed (for example, the average year is 365.2425 days). Use `Scales::Time()` when you want time-aware formatting and parsing.

```
use ;
let mut ft = new;
ft.with_scales;
// 90 seconds -> 1.50 m (minutes)
assert_eq!;
// Quarters (qtr) parse as three-month periods
assert!;
```
For more examples please consult [tests/demo.rs](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/blob/develop/tests/demo.rs)

## Notes

- Months and years are approximate here. For precise calendar math, use a date-time library.
- Very large and very small numbers can lose precision when using `f64`.
- The `with_suffix`method uses the same suffix strings that`try_parse`accepts.

### Suffix vs unit ambiguity

Some short tokens can be ambiguous. For example, the single letter `m` can mean **milli** (a magnitude suffix) or **meter** (a measurement unit) depending on how you configure the `Formatter`:

- `Formatter::new().with_suffix("m")`treats- `m`as milli (scale).
- `Formatter::new().with_units("m")`appends- `m`as the units string (meter).

To avoid ambiguity, prefer longer suffixes or specify units explicitly with `with_units`.

### Case sensitivity

Suffix matching is case-sensitive: `M` (mega) is not the same as `m` (milli). If you want different aliases or case-insensitive parsing, add those aliases to the `Scales` you use.

## parse_or_clamp behavior

The `parse_or_clamp` helper can be used when accepting user-provided suffixes that may be unknown or misspelled. Call it with `clamp = true` to interpret unknown suffixes as the largest available magnitude in the active `Scales`.

Important: when a `Scales` provides an `explicit_map` (for example `Scales::Time()`), `parse_or_clamp` will clamp to the largest multiplier defined in that explicit map rather than assuming a power-of-base value. This ensures consistent behavior for non-power-of-base scales such as time units (where the largest defined unit is `Gyr`).

## Testing and correctness notes

We added a number of focused tests to ensure robust handling of edge-cases:

- Micro sign parsing and optional micro-sign output (tests/micro_sign.rs).
- Forced-suffix behavior including unknown-suffix fallbacks (tests/forced_suffix.rs).
- SI round-trip formatting for new prefixes `R`/`Q`and parsing validation (tests/si_roundtrip.rs).
- Time scale edge cases: months, quarters, parsing case-sensitivity, and clamp behavior (tests/time_edgecases.rs).

If you rely on case-insensitive parsing or custom aliases, construct a `Scales` with the aliases you need and pass it to `Formatter::with_scales`.

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome.

When you add features, please include tests.

## License

See the repository `LICENSE` file for license details.

---

# human_format 1.1.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/human_format/1.1.0

# human-format-rs

Rust Port of human-format from node, formatting numbers for us, while the machines are still at bay.

| Master | Develop |
|---|---|

## What is human_format?

The primary purpose for this crate is to format numbers in a customizable fashion based around magnitudes. It is inspired by the [human-format](https://www.npmjs.com/package/human-format) package and the hope is to ultimately provide an idiomatic rust port.

## Usage

- Add this package as a dependency

```
[]
 = "1.0"
```
- Print some human readable strings

## Examples

```
// 1.00 k
new
    .format);
// 1.34 k
new
    .with_decimals
    .format;
// 1.3 k
new
    .with_decimals
    .format;
// 1.3B
new
    .with_decimals
    .with_separator
    .format;
// 1.00 - k
new
    .with_separator
    .format;
// Define your own scales as you see fit
let mut custom_binary_scales = new;
custom_binary_scales
    .with_base
    .with_suffixes;
// 1.00 kB
new
    .with_scales
    .with_units
    .format;
// 1.00 kiB
new
    .with_scales
    .with_units
    .format;
```
For more examples please consult [tests/demo.rs](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/blob/master/tests/demo.rs)

---

# human_format 1.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/human_format/latest/source/changelog.md

#Changelog
All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](http://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/)
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](http://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
##[Unreleased]
##[1.2.1] - 2026-01-16
###Fixed
-Binary suffix ki should be Kis - [PR#34](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/pull/34) by [ip1981](https://github.com/ip1981)##[1.2.0] - 2025-12-27
###Added
-New tests for cases out in the wild
-`try_parse` which returns `Result<f64, ParseError>` instead of panicking
-`ParseError` enum with variants for `EmptyInput`, `InvalidNumber`, and `UnknownSuffix`-`parse_or_clamp` convenience method to optionally clamp unknown suffixes to the largest multiplier (now respects `explicit_map` when present)
- Doctests and README snippets demonstrating `try_parse`, binary scales, units and negative numbers
- Support for the newest SI prefixes: `R`/`Q` (ronna/quetta) and `r`/`q` (ronto/quecto)
- Optional micro sign formatting and parsing: accept `µ` and output `µ` when enabled via `Formatter::with_micro_sign(true)`- Forced suffix formatting: `Formatter::with_suffix("M")` will scale output to the requested suffix when possible (e.g., `100000 -> 0.10 M`)
- New `Scales::Time()` with explicit time unit multipliers (`ns`, `us`, `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, `w`, `mo`, `qtr`, `y`, `dec`, `c`, `kyr`, `Myr`, `Gyr`, and aliases)
###Changed
-A few tweaks to our build flow to run clippy, and make sure to gate building based on prior dependent actions
- removed verbose flag as it does not appear to be necessary any longer
- Renamed `master` branch to `main`- lower casing si suffixes - [PR#27](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/pull/27) by [jdrouet](https://github.com/jdrouet)- Replaced silent clamping/0.0 multiplier lookup with explicit `try_get_magnitude_multiplier` returning error on unknown suffix
- Refactored parsing internals to centralize numeric/suffix extraction and reduce duplication
- Added edge-case tests (empty input, trailing garbage, comma-decimal behavior, NaN/Infinity, rounding boundaries, and very large magnitudes)
###Removed
-Removed `galvanic-test` as a dependency
##[1.1.0] - 2024-02-16
###Changed
-Format check included in build

# human_format 1.2.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/human_format/latest/source/README.md

```
[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/human_format.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/human_format) [![Documentation](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-rs-red.svg)](https://docs.rs/human_format)
Rust Port of human-format from node, formatting numbers for us, while the machines are still at bay.
`human_format` is a small Rust library that makes numbers easier for people to read. It converts large or small numbers into short strings, like turning `1_000_000` into "1.00 M".
-   -----
Add the crate:
```bash
cargo add human_format
```
Use the formatter:
```rust
use human_format::Formatter;
// Default SI formatting
let s = Formatter::new().format(1000.0);
assert_eq!(s, "1.00 k");
// Control decimals
let s = Formatter::new().with_decimals(1).format(1337.0);
assert_eq!(s, "1.3 k");
```
Use binary scales (base 1024):
```rust
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
let s = Formatter::new().with_scales(Scales::Binary()).format(1024.0);
assert_eq!(s, "1.00 ki");
```
Convert a human-friendly string back to a `f64` with `try_parse`.
```rust
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
let f = Formatter::new();
assert_eq!(f.try_parse("1.00 k").unwrap(), 1000.0);
let mut fb = Formatter::new();
fb.with_scales(Scales::Binary());
assert_eq!(fb.try_parse("1.00 ki").unwrap(), 1024.0);
```
The parser accepts the micro sign `µ` as input.
To force output to a certain suffix, use `with_suffix`. The value is scaled to match that suffix if possible.
```rust
use human_format::Formatter;
let mut f = Formatter::new();
f.with_suffix("M");
assert_eq!(f.format(100_000.0), "0.10 M");
```
If the suffix is not valid for the current `Scales`, the formatter falls back to automatic selection.
Use `with_micro_sign(true)` to show `µ` for micro values in the output.
```rust
use human_format::Formatter;
let mut f = Formatter::new();
f.with_micro_sign(true);
assert_eq!(f.format(0.000001_f64), "1.00 µ");
```
Parsing accepts both `u` and `µ`.
`Scales::Time()` uses a set of explicit unit multipliers for time. It uses average values where needed (for example, the average year is 365.2425 days). Use `Scales::Time()` when you want time-aware formatting and parsing.
```rust
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
let mut ft = Formatter::new();
ft.with_scales(Scales::Time());
// 90 seconds -> 1.50 m (minutes)
assert_eq!(ft.format(90.0), "1.50 m");
// Quarters (qtr) parse as three-month periods
assert!(ft.try_parse("1 qtr").is_ok());
```
For more examples please consult [tests/demo.rs](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/blob/develop/tests/demo.rs)
-   --
Some short tokens can be ambiguous. For example, the single letter `m` can mean **milli** (a magnitude suffix) or **meter** (a measurement unit) depending on how you configure the `Formatter`:
-   -
To avoid ambiguity, prefer longer suffixes or specify units explicitly with `with_units`.
Suffix matching is case-sensitive: `M` (mega) is not the same as `m` (milli). If you want different aliases or case-insensitive parsing, add those aliases to the `Scales` you use.
The `parse_or_clamp` helper can be used when accepting user-provided suffixes that may be unknown or misspelled. Call it with `clamp = true` to interpret unknown suffixes as the largest available magnitude in the active `Scales`.
Important: when a `Scales` provides an `explicit_map` (for example `Scales::Time()`), `parse_or_clamp` will clamp to the largest multiplier defined in that explicit map rather than assuming a power-of-base value. This ensures consistent behavior for non-power-of-base scales such as time units (where the largest defined unit is `Gyr`).
We added a number of focused tests to ensure robust handling of edge-cases:
-   ---
If you rely on case-insensitive parsing or custom aliases, construct a `Scales` with the aliases you need and pass it to `Formatter::with_scales`.
Contributions are welcome.
When you add features, please include tests.
See the repository `LICENSE` file for license details.
```

# human_format - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/human_format/latest/target-redirect/human_format/index.html

## Expand description

`human_format` is a library for formatting numbers into human readable strings. It supports SI, Time and Binary scales out of the box, and allows for custom scales as well.

[§](https://docs.rs#setup)Setup

Add the library to your dependencies listing

`$ cargo add human_format`[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

Print human readable strings from numbers using SI scales by default

```
// "1.00 k"
let tmpStr = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000.0);
// "1.00 M"
let tmpStr2 = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000000.0);
// "1.00 G"
let tmpStr3 = human_format::Formatter::new()
    .format(1000000000.0);
```
If you are so inspired you can even try playing with units and customizing your `Scales`

For more examples you should review the examples on github: [tests/demo.rs](https://github.com/BobGneu/human-format-rs/blob/master/tests/demo.rs)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Formatter](https://docs.rs/struct.Formatter.html)
- Entry point to the library. Use this to handle your formatting needs.
- [Scales](https://docs.rs/struct.Scales.html)
- Provide a customized scaling scheme for your own modeling.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Parse](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)- Error
- Errors returned by parsing operations.

[125](https://docs.rs#125)
[126](https://docs.rs#126)    /// Formats the number into a string
[127](https://docs.rs#127)    pub fn format(&self, value: f64) -> String {
[128](https://docs.rs#128)        // Handle non-finite values explicitly to avoid loops in scaling logic
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        if value.is_nan() {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)            return "NaN".to_owned();
[131](https://docs.rs#131)        }
[132](https://docs.rs#132)
[133](https://docs.rs#133)        if value < 0.0 {
[134](https://docs.rs#134)            return format!("-{}", self.format(-value));
[135](https://docs.rs#135)        }
[136](https://docs.rs#136)
[137](https://docs.rs#137)        if value.is_infinite() {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)            return "inf".to_owned();
[139](https://docs.rs#139)        }
[140](https://docs.rs#140)
[141](https://docs.rs#141)        // If a forced suffix is provided, attempt to scale to that suffix
[142](https://docs.rs#142)        let scaled_value = if !self.forced_suffix.is_empty() {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)            // normalize micro sign in forced suffix when looking up
[144](https://docs.rs#144)            let lookup = self.forced_suffix.replace('\u{00B5}', "u");
[145](https://docs.rs#145)            match self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&lookup) {
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                Ok(mult) => ScaledValue {
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                    value: value / mult,
[148](https://docs.rs#148)                    suffix: self.forced_suffix.clone(),
[149](https://docs.rs#149)                },
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                Err(_) => self.scales.to_scaled_value(value),
[151](https://docs.rs#151)            }
[152](https://docs.rs#152)        } else {
[153](https://docs.rs#153)            self.scales.to_scaled_value(value)
[154](https://docs.rs#154)        };
[155](https://docs.rs#155)
[156](https://docs.rs#156)        let out_suffix = if self.use_micro_sign && scaled_value.suffix == "u" {
[157](https://docs.rs#157)            "µ".to_owned()
[158](https://docs.rs#158)        } else {
[159](https://docs.rs#159)            scaled_value.suffix.clone()
[160](https://docs.rs#160)        };
[161](https://docs.rs#161)
[162](https://docs.rs#162)        format!(
[163](https://docs.rs#163)            "{:.width$}{}{}{}",
[164](https://docs.rs#164)            scaled_value.value,
[165](https://docs.rs#165)            self.separator,
[166](https://docs.rs#166)            out_suffix,
[167](https://docs.rs#167)            self.forced_units,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)            width = self.decimals
[169](https://docs.rs#169)        )
[170](https://docs.rs#170)    }
[171](https://docs.rs#171)
[172](https://docs.rs#172)    /// Parse a string back into a float value.
[173](https://docs.rs#173)    ///
[174](https://docs.rs#174)    /// This convenience wrapper unwraps the result of `try_parse` and will panic
[175](https://docs.rs#175)    /// on malformed input. It is feature-gated behind `panic_parse` so that
[176](https://docs.rs#176)    /// consumers must opt-in to the panicking API via the panic_parse feature.
[177](https://docs.rs#177)    #[cfg(feature = "panic_parse")]
[178](https://docs.rs#178)    #[deprecated(
[179](https://docs.rs#179)        note = "Use `try_parse`, which returns `Result<f64, ParseError>` and does not panic on malformed input"
[180](https://docs.rs#180)    )]
[181](https://docs.rs#181)    pub fn parse(&self, value: &str) -> f64 {
[182](https://docs.rs#182)        self.try_parse(value).unwrap()
[183](https://docs.rs#183)    }
[184](https://docs.rs#184)
[185](https://docs.rs#185)    /// Attempt to parse a string back into a float value.
[186](https://docs.rs#186)    ///
[187](https://docs.rs#187)    /// Examples:
[188](https://docs.rs#188)    ///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)    /// ```rust
[190](https://docs.rs#190)    /// use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
[191](https://docs.rs#191)    /// // SI example
[192](https://docs.rs#192)    /// let f = Formatter::new();
[193](https://docs.rs#193)    /// assert_eq!(f.try_parse("1.00 k").unwrap(), 1000.0);
[194](https://docs.rs#194)    /// // Binary scales (Ki = 1024)
[195](https://docs.rs#195)    /// let mut fbin = Formatter::new();
[196](https://docs.rs#196)    /// fbin.with_scales(Scales::Binary());
[197](https://docs.rs#197)    /// assert_eq!(fbin.try_parse("1.00 Ki").unwrap(), 1024.0);
[198](https://docs.rs#198)    /// // Units specified via with_units() are automatically stripped from input
[199](https://docs.rs#199)    /// let mut funit = Formatter::new();
[200](https://docs.rs#200)    /// funit.with_units("B");
[201](https://docs.rs#201)    /// assert_eq!(funit.try_parse("1.00 kB").unwrap(), 1000.0);
[202](https://docs.rs#202)    /// // Negative numbers
[203](https://docs.rs#203)    /// assert_eq!(Formatter::new().try_parse("-1.0 k").unwrap(), -1000.0);
[204](https://docs.rs#204)    /// // Invalid input
[205](https://docs.rs#205)    /// assert!(Formatter::new().try_parse("bad input").is_err());
[206](https://docs.rs#206)    /// ```
[207](https://docs.rs#207)    pub fn try_parse(&self, value: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[208](https://docs.rs#208)        let (number_str, suffix) = self.parse_components(value)?;
[209](https://docs.rs#209)        let number = number_str
[210](https://docs.rs#210)            .parse::<f64>()
[211](https://docs.rs#211)            .map_err(ParseError::InvalidNumber)?;
[212](https://docs.rs#212)        let magnitude_multiplier = self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&suffix)?;
[213](https://docs.rs#213)
[214](https://docs.rs#214)        Ok(number * magnitude_multiplier)
[215](https://docs.rs#215)    }
[216](https://docs.rs#216)
[217](https://docs.rs#217)    fn parse_components(&self, value: &str) -> Result<(String, String), ParseError> {
[218](https://docs.rs#218)        // Remove forced units if present
[219](https://docs.rs#219)        let value = value
[220](https://docs.rs#220)            .trim()
[221](https://docs.rs#221)            .trim_end_matches(&self.forced_units)
[222](https://docs.rs#222)            .to_string();
[223](https://docs.rs#223)
[224](https://docs.rs#224)        // Extract leading number (allow sign and decimal)
[225](https://docs.rs#225)        let mut number = String::new();
[226](https://docs.rs#226)        for (i, c) in value.chars().enumerate() {
[227](https://docs.rs#227)            if c.is_ascii_digit() || c == '.' || (c == '-' && i == 0) {
[228](https://docs.rs#228)                number.push(c);
[229](https://docs.rs#229)            } else {
[230](https://docs.rs#230)                break;
[231](https://docs.rs#231)            }
[232](https://docs.rs#232)        }
[233](https://docs.rs#233)
[234](https://docs.rs#234)        if number.is_empty() {
[235](https://docs.rs#235)            return Err(ParseError::EmptyInput);
[236](https://docs.rs#236)        }
[237](https://docs.rs#237)
[238](https://docs.rs#238)        let suffix = value
[239](https://docs.rs#239)            .trim_start_matches(&number)
[240](https://docs.rs#240)            .trim_start_matches(&self.separator)
[241](https://docs.rs#241)            .to_string();
[242](https://docs.rs#242)
[243](https://docs.rs#243)        // Normalize common variants: acceptance of micro sign 'µ'
[244](https://docs.rs#244)        let suffix = suffix.replace('\u{00B5}', "u");
[245](https://docs.rs#245)
[246](https://docs.rs#246)        Ok((number, suffix))
[247](https://docs.rs#247)    }
[248](https://docs.rs#248)
[249](https://docs.rs#249)    /// Parse a string and optionally clamp unknown suffixes to the largest suffix multiplier.
[250](https://docs.rs#250)    ///
[251](https://docs.rs#251)    /// If `clamp` is `false`, this behaves like `try_parse` and returns an error on unknown suffixes.
[252](https://docs.rs#252)    /// If `clamp` is `true`, unknown suffixes will be interpreted as the largest available suffix.
[253](https://docs.rs#253)    ///
[254](https://docs.rs#254)    /// Examples:
[255](https://docs.rs#255)    ///
[256](https://docs.rs#256)    /// ```rust
[257](https://docs.rs#257)    /// use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
[258](https://docs.rs#258)    /// let f = Formatter::new();
[259](https://docs.rs#259)    /// // Unknown suffix errors when clamp == false
[260](https://docs.rs#260)    /// assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", false).is_err());
[261](https://docs.rs#261)    /// // Unknown suffix clamps to largest suffix multiplier when clamp == true
[262](https://docs.rs#262)    /// assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", true).is_ok());
[263](https://docs.rs#263)    /// // Binary example with units
[264](https://docs.rs#264)    /// let mut fb = Formatter::new();
[265](https://docs.rs#265)    /// fb.with_scales(Scales::Binary()).with_units("B");
[266](https://docs.rs#266)    /// assert_eq!(fb.parse_or_clamp("1.0 KiB", false).unwrap(), 1024.0);
[267](https://docs.rs#267)    /// // Negative number with clamp
[268](https://docs.rs#268)    /// assert_eq!(Formatter::new().parse_or_clamp("-1.0 k", true).unwrap(), -1000.0);
[269](https://docs.rs#269)    /// ```
[270](https://docs.rs#270)    pub fn parse_or_clamp(&self, value: &str, clamp: bool) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[271](https://docs.rs#271)        let (number_str, suffix) = self.parse_components(value)?;
[272](https://docs.rs#272)        let number = number_str
[273](https://docs.rs#273)            .parse::<f64>()
[274](https://docs.rs#274)            .map_err(ParseError::InvalidNumber)?;
[275](https://docs.rs#275)
[276](https://docs.rs#276)        match self.scales.try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&suffix) {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)            Ok(mult) => Ok(number * mult),
[278](https://docs.rs#278)            Err(ParseError::UnknownSuffix(_)) if clamp => {
[279](https://docs.rs#279)                // If scales has an explicit_map (e.g., Time), clamp to the
[280](https://docs.rs#280)                // largest explicit multiplier rather than assuming a power of
[281](https://docs.rs#281)                // `base` matching the last suffix index.
[282](https://docs.rs#282)                if let Some(map) = &self.scales.explicit_map
[283](https://docs.rs#283)                    && !map.is_empty()
[284](https://docs.rs#284)                {
[285](https://docs.rs#285)                    let max_mult = map.values().copied().fold(f64::NEG_INFINITY, f64::max);
[286](https://docs.rs#286)                    return Ok(number * max_mult);
[287](https://docs.rs#287)                }
[288](https://docs.rs#288)
[289](https://docs.rs#289)                let last_index = self.scales.suffixes.len().saturating_sub(1);
[290](https://docs.rs#290)                let mult = (self.scales.base as f64).powi(last_index as i32);
[291](https://docs.rs#291)
[292](https://docs.rs#292)                Ok(number * mult)
[293](https://docs.rs#293)            }
[294](https://docs.rs#294)            Err(e) => Err(e),
[295](https://docs.rs#295)        }
[296](https://docs.rs#296)    }
[297](https://docs.rs#297)}
[298](https://docs.rs#298)
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// Errors returned by parsing operations.
[300](https://docs.rs#300)#[derive(Debug)]
[301](https://docs.rs#301)pub enum ParseError {
[302](https://docs.rs#302)    EmptyInput,
[303](https://docs.rs#303)    InvalidNumber(std::num::ParseFloatError),
[304](https://docs.rs#304)    UnknownSuffix(String),
[305](https://docs.rs#305)}
[306](https://docs.rs#306)
[307](https://docs.rs#307)impl PartialEq for ParseError {
[308](https://docs.rs#308)    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
[309](https://docs.rs#309)        match (self, other) {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)            (ParseError::EmptyInput, ParseError::EmptyInput) => true,
[311](https://docs.rs#311)            // Note: `ParseFloatError` does not implement `PartialEq` on stable Rust.
[312](https://docs.rs#312)            // We therefore treat all `InvalidNumber(_)` variants as equal to each other,
[313](https://docs.rs#313)            // ignoring the inner `ParseFloatError`.
[314](https://docs.rs#314)            (ParseError::InvalidNumber(_), ParseError::InvalidNumber(_)) => true,
[315](https://docs.rs#315)            (ParseError::UnknownSuffix(a), ParseError::UnknownSuffix(b)) => a == b,
[316](https://docs.rs#316)            _ => false,
[317](https://docs.rs#317)        }
[318](https://docs.rs#318)    }
[319](https://docs.rs#319)}
[320](https://docs.rs#320)
[321](https://docs.rs#321)impl std::fmt::Display for ParseError {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
[323](https://docs.rs#323)        match self {
[324](https://docs.rs#324)            ParseError::EmptyInput => write!(f, "Empty input"),
[325](https://docs.rs#325)            ParseError::InvalidNumber(e) => write!(f, "Invalid number: {}", e),
[326](https://docs.rs#326)            ParseError::UnknownSuffix(s) => write!(f, "Unknown suffix: {}", s),
[327](https://docs.rs#327)        }
[328](https://docs.rs#328)    }
[329](https://docs.rs#329)}

[404](https://docs.rs#404)    /// Instantiates a new `Scales` for time units.
[405](https://docs.rs#405)    ///
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// This maps common time suffixes to multipliers in seconds.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    #[allow(non_snake_case)]
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    pub fn Time() -> Self {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)        use std::collections::HashMap;
[410](https://docs.rs#410)
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        let mut map: HashMap<String, f64> = HashMap::new();
[412](https://docs.rs#412)        map.insert("ns".to_owned(), 1e-9);
[413](https://docs.rs#413)        map.insert("us".to_owned(), 1e-6);
[414](https://docs.rs#414)        map.insert("ms".to_owned(), 1e-3);
[415](https://docs.rs#415)        map.insert("s".to_owned(), 1.0);
[416](https://docs.rs#416)        map.insert("m".to_owned(), 60.0);
[417](https://docs.rs#417)        map.insert("h".to_owned(), 3600.0);
[418](https://docs.rs#418)        map.insert("d".to_owned(), 86400.0);
[419](https://docs.rs#419)        map.insert("w".to_owned(), 604800.0);
[420](https://docs.rs#420)
[421](https://docs.rs#421)        // longer period units using average definitions
[422](https://docs.rs#422)        let year_secs = 365.2425 * 86400.0; // average Gregorian year
[423](https://docs.rs#423)        let month_secs = year_secs / 12.0; // average month
[424](https://docs.rs#424)
[425](https://docs.rs#425)        map.insert("mo".to_owned(), month_secs);
[426](https://docs.rs#426)        map.insert("month".to_owned(), month_secs);
[427](https://docs.rs#427)
[428](https://docs.rs#428)        // quarters: three-month periods
[429](https://docs.rs#429)        map.insert("qtr".to_owned(), 3.0 * month_secs);
[430](https://docs.rs#430)        map.insert("y".to_owned(), year_secs);
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        map.insert("yr".to_owned(), year_secs);
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        map.insert("year".to_owned(), year_secs);
[433](https://docs.rs#433)
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        map.insert("dec".to_owned(), 10.0 * year_secs);
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        map.insert("decade".to_owned(), 10.0 * year_secs);
[436](https://docs.rs#436)
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        map.insert("c".to_owned(), 100.0 * year_secs);
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        map.insert("century".to_owned(), 100.0 * year_secs);
[439](https://docs.rs#439)
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        map.insert("kyr".to_owned(), 1000.0 * year_secs); // millennium (kilo-year)
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        map.insert("millennium".to_owned(), 1000.0 * year_secs);
[442](https://docs.rs#442)
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        map.insert("Myr".to_owned(), 1.0e6 * year_secs);
[444](https://docs.rs#444)
[445](https://docs.rs#445)        map.insert("Gyr".to_owned(), 1.0e9 * year_secs);
[446](https://docs.rs#446)
[447](https://docs.rs#447)        Scales {
[448](https://docs.rs#448)            base: 1,
[449](https://docs.rs#449)            suffixes: vec![],
[450](https://docs.rs#450)            suffixes_neg: vec![],
[451](https://docs.rs#451)            explicit_map: Some(map),
[452](https://docs.rs#452)        }
[453](https://docs.rs#453)    }

[461](https://docs.rs#461)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)    /// Sets the suffixes listing appropriately
[463](https://docs.rs#463)    pub fn with_suffixes(&mut self, suffixes: Vec<&str>) -> &mut Self {
[464](https://docs.rs#464)        self.suffixes = Vec::new();
[465](https://docs.rs#465)
[466](https://docs.rs#466)        for suffix in suffixes {
[467](https://docs.rs#467)            // This should be to_owned to be clear about intent.
[468](https://docs.rs#468)            // https://users.rust-lang.org/t/to-string-vs-to-owned-for-string-literals/1441/6
[469](https://docs.rs#469)            self.suffixes.push(suffix.to_owned());
[470](https://docs.rs#470)        }
[471](https://docs.rs#471)
[472](https://docs.rs#472)        self
[473](https://docs.rs#473)    }
[474](https://docs.rs#474)
[475](https://docs.rs#475)    fn try_get_magnitude_multiplier(&self, value: &str) -> Result<f64, ParseError> {
[476](https://docs.rs#476)        // If an explicit mapping exists (e.g., time units), prefer it
[477](https://docs.rs#477)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map
[478](https://docs.rs#478)            && let Some(val) = map.get(value)
[479](https://docs.rs#479)        {
[480](https://docs.rs#480)            return Ok(*val);
[481](https://docs.rs#481)        }
[482](https://docs.rs#482)
[483](https://docs.rs#483)        // positive suffixes
[484](https://docs.rs#484)        if let Some((idx, _)) = self.suffixes.iter().enumerate().find(|(_, x)| x == &value) {
[485](https://docs.rs#485)            return Ok((self.base as f64).powi(idx as i32));
[486](https://docs.rs#486)        }
[487](https://docs.rs#487)
[488](https://docs.rs#488)        // negative suffixes (fractions)
[489](https://docs.rs#489)        if let Some((idx, _)) = self
[490](https://docs.rs#490)            .suffixes_neg
[491](https://docs.rs#491)            .iter()
[492](https://docs.rs#492)            .enumerate()
[493](https://docs.rs#493)            .find(|(_, x)| x == &value)
[494](https://docs.rs#494)        {
[495](https://docs.rs#495)            // idx 0 corresponds to base^0 (no scaling); idx 1 => base^-1, idx 2 => base^-2
[496](https://docs.rs#496)            let exp = -(idx as i32);
[497](https://docs.rs#497)            return Ok((self.base as f64).powi(exp));
[498](https://docs.rs#498)        }
[499](https://docs.rs#499)
[500](https://docs.rs#500)        // build valid suffix list for error message
[501](https://docs.rs#501)        let mut valid: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
[502](https://docs.rs#502)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map {
[503](https://docs.rs#503)            valid.extend(map.keys().cloned());
[504](https://docs.rs#504)        }
[505](https://docs.rs#505)
[506](https://docs.rs#506)        valid.extend(
[507](https://docs.rs#507)            self.suffixes
[508](https://docs.rs#508)                .iter()
[509](https://docs.rs#509)                .filter(|x| !x.trim().is_empty())
[510](https://docs.rs#510)                .cloned(),
[511](https://docs.rs#511)        );
[512](https://docs.rs#512)
[513](https://docs.rs#513)        valid.extend(
[514](https://docs.rs#514)            self.suffixes_neg
[515](https://docs.rs#515)                .iter()
[516](https://docs.rs#516)                .filter(|x| !x.trim().is_empty())
[517](https://docs.rs#517)                .cloned(),
[518](https://docs.rs#518)        );
[519](https://docs.rs#519)
[520](https://docs.rs#520)        Err(ParseError::UnknownSuffix(format!(
[521](https://docs.rs#521)            "{}; valid suffixes are: {}",
[522](https://docs.rs#522)            value,
[523](https://docs.rs#523)            valid.join(", ")
[524](https://docs.rs#524)        )))
[525](https://docs.rs#525)    }
[526](https://docs.rs#526)
[527](https://docs.rs#527)    fn to_scaled_value(&self, value: f64) -> ScaledValue {
[528](https://docs.rs#528)        let mut index: usize = 0;
[529](https://docs.rs#529)        let base: f64 = self.base as f64;
[530](https://docs.rs#530)        let mut value = value;
[531](https://docs.rs#531)
[532](https://docs.rs#532)        // Prevent infinite loops for non-finite values and cap index to available suffixes
[533](https://docs.rs#533)        let last_index = self.suffixes.len().saturating_sub(1);
[534](https://docs.rs#534)        let last_neg = self.suffixes_neg.len().saturating_sub(1);
[535](https://docs.rs#535)
[536](https://docs.rs#536)        // If explicit map provided (e.g., Time), prefer selecting suffix from it
[537](https://docs.rs#537)        if let Some(map) = &self.explicit_map {
[538](https://docs.rs#538)            // Build vector of (suffix, multiplier) and sort descending by multiplier
[539](https://docs.rs#539)            let mut entries: Vec<(String, f64)> =
[540](https://docs.rs#540)                map.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), *v)).collect();
[541](https://docs.rs#541)            entries.sort_by(|a, b| b.1.partial_cmp(&a.1).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal));
[542](https://docs.rs#542)
[543](https://docs.rs#543)            if value > 0.0 {
[544](https://docs.rs#544)                for (suf, mult) in entries.iter() {
[545](https://docs.rs#545)                    if value >= *mult {
[546](https://docs.rs#546)                        return ScaledValue {
[547](https://docs.rs#547)                            value: value / *mult,
[548](https://docs.rs#548)                            suffix: suf.clone(),
[549](https://docs.rs#549)                        };
[550](https://docs.rs#550)                    }
[551](https://docs.rs#551)                }
[552](https://docs.rs#552)
[553](https://docs.rs#553)                // If smaller than smallest multiplier, use smallest (e.g., ns)
[554](https://docs.rs#554)                if let Some((suf, mult)) = entries.last() {
[555](https://docs.rs#555)                    return ScaledValue {
[556](https://docs.rs#556)                        value: value / *mult,
[557](https://docs.rs#557)                        suffix: suf.clone(),
[558](https://docs.rs#558)                    };
[559](https://docs.rs#559)                }
[560](https://docs.rs#560)            }
[561](https://docs.rs#561)        }
[562](https://docs.rs#562)
[563](https://docs.rs#563)        if value >= base {
[564](https://docs.rs#564)            while value >= base && index < last_index {
[565](https://docs.rs#565)                value /= base;
[566](https://docs.rs#566)                index += 1;
[567](https://docs.rs#567)            }
[568](https://docs.rs#568)
[569](https://docs.rs#569)            ScaledValue {
[570](https://docs.rs#570)                value,
[571](https://docs.rs#571)                suffix: self.suffixes[index].to_owned(),
[572](https://docs.rs#572)            }
[573](https://docs.rs#573)        } else if value > 0.0 && value < 1.0 {
[574](https://docs.rs#574)            // Use negative prefixes for fractional values
[575](https://docs.rs#575)            let mut neg_idx: usize = 0;
[576](https://docs.rs#576)            while value < 1.0 && neg_idx < last_neg {
[577](https://docs.rs#577)                value *= base;
[578](https://docs.rs#578)                neg_idx += 1;
[579](https://docs.rs#579)            }
[580](https://docs.rs#580)
[581](https://docs.rs#581)            ScaledValue {
[582](https://docs.rs#582)                value,
[583](https://docs.rs#583)                suffix: self.suffixes_neg[neg_idx].to_owned(),
[584](https://docs.rs#584)            }
[585](https://docs.rs#585)        } else {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)            ScaledValue {
[587](https://docs.rs#587)                value,
[588](https://docs.rs#588)                suffix: self.suffixes[0].to_owned(),
[589](https://docs.rs#589)            }
[590](https://docs.rs#590)        }
[591](https://docs.rs#591)    }
[592](https://docs.rs#592)}

#### pub fn [with_separator](https://docs.rs#method.with_separator)(&mut self, separator: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> &mut Self

Sets the separator value for formatting the string.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#120-124)#### pub fn [with_micro_sign](https://docs.rs#method.with_micro_sign)(&mut self, enable: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#120-124)

#### pub fn [with_micro_sign](https://docs.rs#method.with_micro_sign)(&mut self, enable: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)) -> &mut Self

Enable using the micro sign `µ` in formatted output when fractional suffix is `u`.

Attempt to parse a string back into a float value.

Examples:

```
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
// SI example
let f = Formatter::new();
assert_eq!(f.try_parse("1.00 k").unwrap(), 1000.0);
// Binary scales (Ki = 1024)
let mut fbin = Formatter::new();
fbin.with_scales(Scales::Binary());
assert_eq!(fbin.try_parse("1.00 Ki").unwrap(), 1024.0);
// Units specified via with_units() are automatically stripped from input
let mut funit = Formatter::new();
funit.with_units("B");
assert_eq!(funit.try_parse("1.00 kB").unwrap(), 1000.0);
// Negative numbers
assert_eq!(Formatter::new().try_parse("-1.0 k").unwrap(), -1000.0);
// Invalid input
assert!(Formatter::new().try_parse("bad input").is_err());
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#270-296)#### pub fn [parse_or_clamp](https://docs.rs#method.parse_or_clamp)(
    &self,
    value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    clamp: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/human_format/lib.rs.html#270-296)

#### pub fn [parse_or_clamp](https://docs.rs#method.parse_or_clamp)(
    &self,
    value: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    clamp: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html), [ParseError](https://docs.rs/enum.ParseError.html)>

Parse a string and optionally clamp unknown suffixes to the largest suffix multiplier.

If `clamp` is `false`, this behaves like `try_parse` and returns an error on unknown suffixes.
If `clamp` is `true`, unknown suffixes will be interpreted as the largest available suffix.

Examples:

```
use human_format::{Formatter, Scales};
let f = Formatter::new();
// Unknown suffix errors when clamp == false
assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", false).is_err());
// Unknown suffix clamps to largest suffix multiplier when clamp == true
assert!(f.parse_or_clamp("1.0 DN", true).is_ok());
// Binary example with units
let mut fb = Formatter::new();
fb.with_scales(Scales::Binary()).with_units("B");
assert_eq!(fb.parse_or_clamp("1.0 KiB", false).unwrap(), 1024.0);
// Negative number with clamp
assert_eq!(Formatter::new().parse_or_clamp("-1.0 k", true).unwrap(), -1000.0);
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

Documentation:

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [arg](https://docs.rs/macro.arg.html)
- Create an `Arg`
- [command](https://docs.rs/macro.command.html)- `cargo`
- Allows you to build the `Command`instance from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_authors.html)- authors - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the authors for the command from your Cargo.toml at
compile time in the form:
`"author1 lastname <author1@example.com>:author2 lastname <author2@example.com>"`
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_description.html)- description - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the description from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_name.html)- name - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the name from your Cargo.toml at compile time.
- [crate_](https://docs.rs/macro.crate_version.html)- version - `cargo`
- Allows you to pull the version from your Cargo.toml at compile time as
`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH_PKGVERSION_PRE`
- [value_](https://docs.rs/macro.value_parser.html)- parser
- Select a `ValueParser`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Arg](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- The abstract representation of a command line argument. Used to set all the options and relationships that define a valid argument for the program.
- [ArgGroup](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgGroup.html)
- Specifies a logical group of [arguments](https://docs.rs/struct.Arg.html)
- [ArgMatches](https://docs.rs/struct.ArgMatches.html)
- Container for parse results.

- Build a command-line interface.

- `Arg`- `ArgGroup`

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- Behavior of arguments when they are encountered while parsing
- [Color](https://docs.rs/enum.ColorChoice.html)- Choice
- Represents the color preferences for program output
- [Value](https://docs.rs/enum.ValueHint.html)- Hint
- Provide shell with hint on how to complete an argument.

- Parse a set of arguments into a user-defined container.

- Create a `Command`
- [From](https://docs.rs/trait.FromArgMatches.html)- ArgMatches
- Converts an instance of `ArgMatches`
- [Parser](https://docs.rs/trait.Parser.html)
- Parse command-line arguments into `Self`.
- [Subcommand](https://docs.rs/trait.Subcommand.html)
- Parse a sub-command into a user-defined enum.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/trait.ValueEnum.html)- Enum
- Parse arguments into enums.

- Converts an instance of `ArgMatches`

- Parse a sub-command into a user-defined enum.

- Parse arguments into enums.
